title: TRACE: Transition-Aware Residual Control for Multi-Objective Materials Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2608.23631v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-objective materials discovery with LLM agents is often limited not only by how many candidates can be proposed, but by how effectively each costly property evaluation informs the next search step. Existing agents mainly store evaluated candidates and their scores, so they know which materials succeeded but not which executable edits caused useful property changes. This makes local refinement difficult when objectives compete and an edit that improves one property may damage another. We propose TRACE, a transition-aware residual control framework that treats evaluated edits as the basic unit of feedback. translated_title: TRACE：面向多目标材料发现的过渡感知残差控制框架
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23631v1 公告类型：新论文  摘要：使用LLM智能体进行多目标材料发现，不仅受限于能提出多少候选材料，还受限于每次昂贵的性质评估如何有效指导下一步搜索。现有智能体主要存储已评估的候选材料及其评分，因此它们知道哪些材料成功了，但不知道哪些可执行的编辑操作导致了有用的性质变化。这使得在目标相互竞争且改善一个性质的编辑可能损害另一个性质时，局部优化变得困难。我们提出TRACE，一种过渡感知的残差控制框架，将已评估的编辑视为反馈的基本单元。TRACE将每次局部优化记录为父编辑-子编辑的过渡，并附有观察到的性质变化，聚合过渡证据以估计可复用的编辑效果，并根据未来编辑预测能力来排序，以减少当前候选的剩余约束违反，同时避免损害已满足的目标。
tldr: TRACE通过将编辑操作作为反馈单元并记录性质变化，实现多目标材料发现中的智能局部优化，从而在平衡冲突目标的同时有效指导搜索。
en_tdlr: TRACE treats edits as feedback units and records property deltas to enable intelligent local refinement in multi-objective materials discovery, balancing conflicting objectives while guiding search effectively.
